description: Migrates all dashboards from the source to the target environment in batches.

action.description: Determines how to handle existing dashboards in the target environment. Options: - 'skip': Skip existing dashboards in the target; new dashboards are processed normally, including shares and ownership. - 'overwrite': Overwrite existing dashboards; shares and ownership will not be migrated. If the dashboard already exists, shares will be retained, but the API user will be set as the new owner. - 'duplicate': Create a duplicate of existing dashboards without migrating shares or ownership. Default: None. Existing dashboards are skipped, and only new ones are migrated. Unless existing dashboards are different owners, shares will be migrated. **Note:** If an existing dashboard in the target environment has a different owner than the user's token running the SDK, the dashboard will be migrated with a new ID, and its shares and ownership will be migrated from the original source dashboard.

republish.description: Whether to republish dashboards after migration. Default: False.

migrate_share.description: Whether to migrate shares for the dashboards. If `True`, shares will be migrated, and ownership migration will be controlled by the `change_ownership` parameter. If `False`, both shares and ownership migration will be skipped. Default: False.

change_ownership.description: Whether to change ownership of the target dashboards. Effective only if `migrate_share` is True. Default: False.

batch_size.description: Number of dashboards to process in each batch. Default: 10.

sleep_time.description: Time (in seconds) to sleep between batches. Default: 10 seconds.

emit.description: Optional callback invoked with structured progress events. If not provided, the method emits no events and only returns a final result. Event payloads follow a consistent shape: - ``type``: str ("started" | "progress" | "warning" | "error" | "completed") - ``step``: str logical step identifier - ``message``: str human-readable message - Additional fields depending on the step (counts, status_code, etc.)

examples.user_query: How can I migrate all dashboards to the target environment, skipping any that already exist?
examples.notes: This call migrates all dashboards from the source to the target environment, skipping any dashboards that already exist in the target. Shares and ownership will not be migrated.

examples.user_query: I want to migrate all dashboards and overwrite any existing ones in the target environment. How can I do that?
examples.notes: This call migrates all dashboards from the source to the target environment, overwriting any existing dashboards in the target. Shares and ownership will not be migrated, and the API user will become the new owner of overwritten dashboards. Dashboards will be republished after migration.

examples.user_query: Can I migrate all dashboards and create duplicates for any that already exist in the target environment?
examples.notes: This call migrates all dashboards from the source to the target environment, creating duplicates for any dashboards that already exist in the target. Shares and ownership will be migrated for the new duplicates.

source_dashboard_ids.description: A list of dashboard IDs from the source environment to fetch shares from.

target_dashboard_ids.description: A list of dashboard IDs from the target environment to apply shares to.

change_ownership.description: Whether to change ownership of the target dashboard. Defaults to False.

examples.notes: This call migrates shares from a single source dashboard (dashboard_abc) to a target dashboard (dashboard_xyz) and updates ownership in the target environment.

examples.user_query: Can I migrate shares for multiple dashboards without changing ownership?
examples.notes: This call migrates shares for three dashboards from the source environment to corresponding dashboards in the target environment without altering ownership.

description: Migrate dashboards from the source to the target environment using Sisense bulk import.

dashboard_ids.description: List of dashboard OIDs to migrate. Provide either `dashboard_ids` or `dashboard_names`.

dashboard_names.description: List of dashboard titles to migrate. Provide either `dashboard_ids` or `dashboard_names`.

action.description: Determines how the target handles conflicts. - None: default Sisense behavior (typically skip existing). - "skip": skip if exists. - "overwrite": overwrite if exists (shares/ownership migration is skipped). - "duplicate": create duplicate (shares/ownership migration is skipped).

republish.description: Whether to republish dashboards after import.

migrate_share.description: If True, attempts to migrate shares (and optionally ownership) after dashboards are created.

change_ownership.description: If True and `migrate_share=True`, attempts to change ownership on the target dashboards.

examples.user_query: How can I migrate dashboards with IDs 'dash123' and 'dash456' to the target environment, skipping any that already exist?
examples.notes: This call migrates the specified dashboards by their IDs, skipping any that already exist in the target environment. Shares and ownership are not migrated, and dashboards are not republished after import.

examples.user_query: I want to migrate dashboards named 'Sales Overview' and 'Marketing Insights' to the target environment, overwriting any existing ones. Can I also republish them after migration?
examples.notes: This call migrates the specified dashboards by their names, overwriting any existing dashboards with the same names in the target environment. The dashboards will also be republished after the migration.

examples.user_query: Can I migrate dashboards with IDs 'dash789' and 'dash101' to the target environment, create duplicates if they already exist, and also migrate shares and ownership?
examples.notes: This call migrates the specified dashboards by their IDs, creating duplicates in the target environment if dashboards with the same IDs already exist. Shares and ownership will also be migrated for the newly created dashboards.
